spans.s:
rāga-dveṣa
(‘attachment and aversion’)
------------------------------------------
The two words राग (attachment) and द्वेष (hatred or aversion) are often used together since the two are, in a way, interconnected. When somebody thwarts a person from fulfilling his desire, born out of राग, it turns into द्वेष or aversion towards that person causing the obstacle.
They are the equivalents of काम (desire) and krodha (anger), the first two of the ariṣaḍvargas (the six enemies of spiritual evolution).

rāga
(‘that which colours,’ ‘attachment’)
------------------------------------------
One of the most commonly used words, ‘rāga’ comes from the root-verb ‘rañj’ (= to colour). Anything that ‘colours’ the मिन्द्, makes it strongly attached, is राग.
The Bhagavadgītā (2.64; 3.34; 14.7) uses this word in the general sense of attachment to anything and that it is caused by the quality called रजस्, the second of the three guṇas.
The Yogasūtras (3.7) of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) describes it as the extreme desire that arises in the मिन्द् after a pleasurable experience, the residual desire to get that pleasure once again and the consequent attachment towards the means of getting it. Along with द्वेष or hatred, it is considered as a great obstacle in the path of spiritual unfoldment.
In the science of मुसिच्, राग is a tune generated by the proper combination of the saptasvaras or the seven fundamental notes. Here, they are called rāgas because they give pleasure to the मिन्द्.
These rāgas are classed as six by the authorities on मुसिच्, though the names differ in the lists given by them. For instance, one list gives them as: Mālava, इन्द्र, Mallāra, Śrīrāga, Vasanta and Hindola.
Each of these rāgas has six feminine associates—called rāgiṇīs—taking their total to thirty six.
Sometimes, depending upon the sentiments produced, the rāgas are also classified as puṁrāga (male), strīrāga (female) and napuṁsakarāga (neuter).
The puṁrāgas produce the sentiments of heroism and wonder; the strīrāgas, of amour and humour; the napuṁsakarāgas, of peace and fear.
See also DVEṢA.

rāgānugabhakti
(‘devotion that follows emotion’)
------------------------------------------
Bhakti or devotion to God has been categorised into several varieties by the various schools of भक्ति Vedānta. Two such are the वैधीभक्ति and the रागानुगभक्ति.
If the former follows the vidhis or the rules set in the śāstras (holy books or scripture), the latter follows just one’s राग or emotional attachment. Hence it can take any form of human emotion towards God, who too may be considered as one’s child or friend or beloved. God also will respond in the same way as towards यशोदा (as her child), अर्जुन (as a friend) or the गोपीस् (as their beloved).
